evidence.detail: rs/N extends the recovered Node base and is stored in Client's dedicated Node list. Its constructor initializes one object-id field to -1, matching an empty/original-object sentinel.

Client resolves the record's plane/x/y plus object-category selector through the recovered Scene API, reads the current scene object tag/config and stores the existing object id, shape and orientation back into the record.

The live client loop decrements two independent countdown fields. When each reaches zero it validates the stored/replacement object definition and invokes the scene-object update routine with the record's coordinates, category, object id, shape and orientation, removing the Node after completion.

The client update/enqueue path searches the list for an existing record with the same plane/x/y/category, creates rs/N when absent, captures the previous scene state, then writes replacement object id/orientation/shape and lifetime/delay values into the record.

Historical 317 client sources expose an exact structural match named SpawnObjectNode: a Node subclass with the same constructor default of -1 and the same queued spawned-object processing pattern. Historical naming is corroborative; exact-v308 behavior is primary authority.

candidates.note: Source-proven historical identity strongly corroborated by exact-v308 scene lookup, replacement state, two countdowns and Node-list lifecycle.
